title: Audit event normalization and compact delta anchors for RBAC + SSO traces
creator: Anita Park
description:
Background:
Redwood needs a single, compact, and queryable audit contract that covers RBAC v2 changes, admin operations, and enriched SSO/SAML context so that: (1) security teams can trace a user action across multi-tenant flows; (2) incident responders can reconstruct state changes with minimal storage; and (3) privacy and retention policies can be enforced deterministically.

Problem statement:
Current audit events are inconsistent across services: some emit full resource snapshots, others emit ad-hoc diffs, and SSO-related events rarely surface the full identity chain (IdP assertion IDs, SAML attributes). This makes lookups and blame analysis slow and increases storage. We need a canonical event shape and a compact delta format that preserves semantic clarity for actor/target/role changes while minimizing token-level size and making queries efficient.

Goals:
- Define a canonical audit event envelope that every service will emit for admin/RBAC/SSO actions.
- Standardize actor and target representation so a single lookup key links to user identity, SSO assertion, and service principal.
- Design a compact delta format for state changes (role grants/revokes, policy edits, group membership) that supports: apply/reverse, human-readable reconstruction, and efficient storage.
- Provide migration and adapter guidance for services that currently emit full snapshots.
- Define acceptance criteria, retention + sampling rules, and privacy redaction hooks.

Proposed canonical event envelope (high level, stringified):
- envelope_id: stable UUID for this audit record
- stream_anchor: monotonic anchor (yyyyMMddHHmmss-xxxx) used for cross-service correlation
- emitted_by: service identifier (e.g., runtime-serving:gpu-3)
- event_type: taxonomy tag (e.g., admin.role.grant, sso.login.assertion_received, rbac.policy.update)
- severity: info|warning|critical
- actor: canonical actor descriptor (see actor model below)
- target: canonical target descriptor (resource canonical id + resource type)
- delta: compact change payload (see delta encoding proposals)
- prior_snapshot_ref: optional anchor or hash referencing prior snapshot for deterministic replay
- human_summary: short natural language summary for dashboards/alerts
- metadata: list of tags/labels (list of strings)
- raw_assertion: optional encrypted pointer to SAML/IdP payload (KMS-wrapped)
- retention_tier: short|standard|long
- sampling_hint: none|partial|redacted
- signature: service-signed HMAC to verify ingestion authenticity

Actor model (canonical fields):
- actor.id: canonical user id (internal) or service principal id
- actor.type: user|service|guest|external-idp
- actor.identity_chain: ordered list of identity anchors as strings (IdP:assertion-id, upstream-proxy-id, delegated-principal-id) -- stored as an array stringified in the event
- actor.ip, actor.user_agent, actor.credential_type (sso/saml/jwt/api_key)

Target model:
- target.id: canonical resource id (tenant-scoped)
- target.type: role|policy|group|route|model
- target.preferred_display: human readable name for product UIs

Delta encoding proposals (compact, line-oriented; payloads are encoded as UTF-8 and gzip+base64 when larger than 1KB):
Option A: Compact operation list (recommended) - grammar as plain text ops to minimize JSON overhead:
  +set path=/roles/123/members value=user:alice  # grant
  -set path=/roles/123/members value=user:bob    # revoke
  replace path=/policy/42/rules value=(cond:...) # policy update
  note: ops recorded in chronological order; apply/reverse algorithm is deterministic and documented in README.

Option B: JSON-patch with semantic normalization - use RFC6902 but normalize ordering, type-coercions, and collapse redundant ops. Larger but compatible with many libraries.

Option C: Field-delta tuples (field, old, new) for quick human diffing. Useful for UI change logs but less compact at scale.

We recommend Option A for most RBAC changes because it is compact and human-readable, and fall back to Option B for complex nested schema edits. All diffs must include an operations_hash (sha256 of the ops text) and a delta_encoding label.

Indexing and lookup strategy:
- Primary lookup keys: envelope_id, stream_anchor, actor.id, target.id, operations_hash.
- For cross-tenant flows include tenant_id in the index.
- Downstream ingestion pipelines (ClickHouse/Kafka consumer) will build materialized views mapping actor -> event anchors and target -> change timeline.

Retention, sampling and redaction:
- Default retention: 90 days for standard events, 365 days for critical admin events.
- Sampling policy: use sampling_hint to allow deterministic sampling per tenant and tenant tier. Example: sample 1/1000 for non-critical automated role syncs.
- Redaction: PII fields (raw_assertion, actor.identity_chain elements with email) must be stored only behind KMS-wrapped pointers or redacted at emission if tenant opts-in. Redaction policy must be deterministic across services to avoid mismatched deltas.

Migration path for existing services:
1) Adapter layer: emit envelope fields and include legacy_payload as raw_snapshot field; set migration=false.
2) Conversion job: nightly consumer that emits compact deltas for historical snapshots and writes prior_snapshot_ref anchors.
3) Strict mode: after 3 cycles, services must switch to emitting compact deltas only for admin/RBAC events.

Acceptance criteria (must pass before feature merge):
- All admin role changes from runtime services produce envelope + compact delta for 90% of events in canary tenant.
- Cross-service trace across SSO login -> role grant -> permission use reconstructs a coherent timeline using stream_anchor and operations_hash.
- CLI tooling can reconstruct human-readable change log from envelope+delta in <250ms for 90th percentile.
- Security review sign-off and integration test validating KMS wrapping of raw_assertion pointer.

Migration and rollout plan (phased):
- Phase 0: Spec review and library (go/python) for delta encoding + canonical actor/target helpers (2 weeks).
- Phase 1: Canary emitters in auth service + runtime-serving for admin.role.grant/ revoke (1 week).
- Phase 2: Expand to platform services and deploy ingestion consumer that materializes actor/target indices (2 weeks).
- Phase 3: Migrate historical snapshots and flip enforcement gate (3 weeks).

Open design questions and trade-offs:
- Do we require every service to sign events with service key (stronger ingestion auth) vs rely on ingestion zone ACL? (security vs operational friction)
- Compact ops (Option A) require service libraries to adopt the grammar; JSON-patch gives compatibility at cost of size.
- How to represent batched changes where a single API call causes hundreds of atomic ops? Use grouped op blocks with batch_id.

Deliverables:
- Draft spec (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/Audit+Normalization+Spec
- Delta encoding reference library (Go/Python): https://github.com/redwood-inference/audit-delta-lib (WIP PR linked below)
- Ingestion consumer PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/4128

Notes on privacy and legal review: Engage Compliance for SAML assertion retention policy. Decision required on whether to store full assertion pointers for 365 days for enterprise tenants.
